title: Outgrowths tend to arise from triangular rather than quadrangular cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Outgrowths tend to arise from triangular rather than quadrangular cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because quadrangular cells subdivide by periclinal walls that strengthen the boundary while triangular cells divide by oblique anticlines, outward growth is greater over triangular cells, so buds and outgrowths tend to arise from triangular rather than quadrangular cells, as is widely seen in cryptogams.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As a direct and immediate consequence of this we might expect a tendency for special outgrowths, or “buds,” to arise from the triangular rather than from the quadrangular cells; and this turns out to be not merely a tendency towards which theoretical considerations point, but a widespread and important factor in the morphology of the cryptogams.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Buds from triangular cells”. Scope: growing points and buds of cryptogams (mosses, liverworts, ferns, algae)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The enrichment of buds over triangular cells is a direct statistical prediction. Some archived developmental imaging can test particular systems, but broad cryptogam coverage and causal separation from polarity are weak.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map cell sidedness, wall orientation, and subsequent bud initiation in cryptogam time series and test whether outgrowths originate disproportionately over triangular cells.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cryptogams are sparsely represented in public lineage-resolved imaging.

Cell topology may correlate with pre-existing developmental polarity.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A preference for outgrowths on triangular cells is a countable bias, and some apical images exist to start the count. Coverage of cryptogams is thin, and the classical anatomical plates are not a clean sample. Position is a serious confound because the cells the claim singles out also occupy the usual bud site.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At cryptogam apices, compare the frequency of buds and other outgrowths on triangular cells with the frequency on quadrangular cells, holding position on the apex constant. A higher outgrowth rate on triangular cells would support the claim; no bias, or a bias toward quadrangular cells, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Triangular cells often sit at the tip, so shape and the position where buds arise are collinear unless position is controlled.

Moss, liverwort, fern and algal apices are not gathered in one shape-by-outgrowth table.
